page: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server instance designed for compute-intensive workloads that require substantial network throughput. Built without a hypervisor layer, it provides direct access to 36 physical cores and 72 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 extensions, AES cryptography, and hardware virtualization through Intel VMX. Memory configuration consists of 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing approximately 2.67 GB of memory per core.

Networking and I/O capabilities are anchored by a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring all persistent and scratch storage to be attached via networked block storage services. Benchmark metrics show strong multi-core processing with a stress-ng score of 67384.33 and a PassMark CPU score of 50868.09, both ranking in the top tier. Uncached memory read bandwidth demonstrates strong throughput at 212.97 GB/sec, alongside strong performance in PassMark database operations and Clang compilation tasks. Conversely, single-thread performance and text generation tasks on large language models register at average to lower-tier levels.

From an operational efficiency perspective, the bare-metal design eliminates virtualization overhead, delivering consistent CPU execution and predictable network latency across all 72 vCPUs. The hardware profile is optimal for distributed high-performance computing, network-intensive clustered applications, large-scale software compilation, and high-concurrency database workloads that rely on high network throughput and dedicated execution threads.
description: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized instance delivering direct access to hardware without hypervisor virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz, it supplies 36 physical cores, 72 vCPUs, and 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It features a 100 Gbps network interface and contains no local storage, directing all disk activity to network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations show top-quartile multi-core processing, strong software compilation performance, and high uncached read memory bandwidth, while single-core processing and LLM text generation remain in average to lower tiers. The high core count combined with 100 Gbps bandwidth makes c5n.metal suitable for network-bound compute tasks, large-scale Clang build pipelines, distributed clustered simulations, and transactional database services requiring predictable thread scheduling.
